division.heading: Lawyers’ Charges, Retainer Agreements and Right of Review

operative_text.controlling:
10.14(1)  If a lawyer is served with notice of an appointment for
a review of the lawyer’s charges or retainer agreement, or both,
the lawyer must file
(a) a copy of the account, appropriately signed, in respect of
which the client seeks a review,
(b) a copy of any time records upon which the account is
based, and
(c) a copy of any retainer agreement between the lawyer and
the client whether or not the lawyer intends to rely on
them.
(2)  The documents must be filed 5 days or more before the
appointment date or within any other period specified by a review
officer, and the review officer may vary the period before or after
the time limit has passed.
(3)  If the lawyer does not comply with this rule, the lawyer forfeits
the right to payment of the lawyer’s charges in any account that is
the subject of a review unless the review officer otherwise directs.

BOOK_A.title: Client-Obtained Appointment: Lawyer’s Responsibility
BOOK_A.commentary:
The "forfeiture" in subrule (3) should not be mechanical and automatic, and sometimes a
very brief adjournment may enable production of the missing information, in which case the fault
should be excused.²
If a party seeks costs, especially full-indemnity costs, it must provide at the beginning of the
review by a review ofﬁcer a bill of costs, a statement of account, or other evidence of the amounts
claimed.³
A client objecting to his or her lawyer’s bill must give particulars of the objections.⁴

BOOK_B.title: Client-obtained appointment: lawyer's responsibility

commentary.text: Rule 10.14 See Alberta Rules of Court, Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 10.14. Agreements as to Interest If lawyers ever do make an agreement in advance with their client that interest will be charged and paid, I would think such an agreement would have to be deposited with the taxing officer pursuant to the provisions of Rule 646. Fowle, Todd & Co. v. Klassen (1981), 31 A.R. 494 (Q.B.), at 497, per Cavanagh J.

BOOK_C.title: Client-obtained appointment: lawyer’s responsibility

commentary.text:
In assessing whether they should exercise their discretion to protect a lawyer from forfeiture under rule 10.14, the review officer should consider whether a short adjournment would remedy the issue.An adjournment could be as short as a few minutes. The review officer should balance potential prejudice to the client with providing them the basic tools needed to determine whether the lawyer’s account was reasonable. Moore v. Hildebrand, [2013] A.J. No. 270, 2013 ABQB 167 at para. 22 (Alta. Q.B.).
The foundational rules (Part 1) cannot override the specific requirement in rule 10.14 to file a retainer agreement. Moore v. Hildebrand, [2013] A.J. No. 270, 2013 ABQB 167 at para. 16 (Alta. Q.B.). The quickest way at the least expense for the review officer to get background context for a fee dispute is to examine, before the review hearing, the basic materials, including the retainer agreement, that will establish the right to recovery. Moore v. Hildebrand, [2013] A.J. No. 270, 2013 ABQB 167 at para. 17 (Alta. Q.B.). A lawyer’s contravention of rule 10.14 could be a sufficient basis on which to deny costs and require payment to the former client costs for appearances before the review officer and on

The first paragraph agrees with Book A's note (a short adjournment; the forfeiture in subrule (3) is not mechanical), which cites the same case, Moore v. Hildebrand 2013 ABQB 167; the words 'the review officer should consider whether a short adjournment would remedy the issue.An adjournment could be as short as a few minutes' have no space after the full stop (as printed). The second paragraph ('The foundational rules (Part 1) cannot override the specific requirement in rule 10.14 to file a retainer agreement', Moore para 16; 'The quickest way at the least expense for the review officer to get background context ... is to examine, before the review hearing, the basic materials, including the retainer agreement', Moore para 17) is consistent with official 10.14(1)(c) (a copy of any retainer agreement, 'whether or not the lawyer intends to rely on' it); the paragraph pinpoints (paras 22, 16 and 17) are not checked against Moore, which neither Book A nor Book B quotes. The passage is kept as printed (flagged).
